Silver nanowires have an average diameter of 19.5 ± 1.6 nm and length of 18.2 ± 7.3 µm.
AgNWs are coated mainly on the surface of cellulose papers with decreasing density through thickness.
A single dip-coating cycle yields an in-plane electrical conductivity of 0.34 S/cm.
Multiple dip-coating cycles increase conductivity up to 67.51 S/cm.
The highest conductivity paper contains only 0.53 vol % AgNWs.
EMI shielding effectiveness reaches approximately 48.6 dB at 1 GHz.
Neat cellulose paper has electrical conductivity around 10^-11 S/cm.
SEM and TEM imaging confirm the morphology and crystalline structure of AgNWs.
FT-IR spectra indicate specific interactions between polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and AgNWs.
Crystalline boundaries in AgNWs are surrounded by PVP chains.
The cellulose paper structure facilitates the formation of a conductive AgNW network.
Electrical conductivity is anisotropic, higher in-plane than through thickness.
The dip-coating process is efficient and facile for fabricating AgNW/cellulose papers.
AgNW/cellulose papers are flexible and lightweight.
These papers can serve as conductive components and EMI shielding elements in advanced applications.
